build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player character clings to walls on contact and slides slowly downward. Pressing jump while clinging launches the character away from the wall with directional control. Score 0 if wall interaction is absent or the character passes through walls.

A directional dash consumes a single charge, propelling the character at high speed in the aimed direction. The charge resets on landing or wall-grab, creating a commit-recover rhythm. Score 0 if no dash exists or dash has no resource cost.

Hazards (spikes, pits, moving obstacles) kill the player instantly on contact and respawn them at the room entrance with no loading delay. The death-respawn loop is near-instantaneous. Score 0 if hazards do not kill or respawn has significant delay.

Rooms are screen-sized and clearing one scrolls or transitions the camera to the next room seamlessly. Progression through rooms is linear within a chapter. Score 0 if rooms do not transition or the game is a single continuous level.

Multiple chapters (at least 3) are present, each introducing distinct hazard types (e.g., wind, crumbling walls, gravity flips, timed gates). Completing a chapter unlocks the next. Score 0 if only one chapter or hazard type exists.

Each chapter contains at least 5 distinct rooms with unique layouts that test wall-climb and dash in different configurations. Rooms within a chapter feel varied, not repetitive. Score 0 if fewer than 5 rooms exist or all rooms share identical layouts.

At least 4 distinct hazard types are present across the game (spikes, moving saws, crumbling platforms, wind currents, timed gates, gravity zones, etc.) each requiring different player responses. Score 0 if only one hazard type exists.

A chapter-select or hub screen allows replaying completed chapters. Death counter and best-time tracking per chapter are visible and persist between sessions. Score 0 if no chapter select or tracking exists.

Final rooms in chapters combine multiple hazard types from that chapter into a culminating challenge that tests mastery. These rooms are noticeably harder and more complex than earlier rooms. Score 0 if no difficulty escalation exists within chapters.
Chapter completion shows a results screen with death count, time taken, and a rating or grade. The results reflect actual performance during that chapter. Score 0 if no results screen exists.
A styled title screen shows the game name, chapter-select option, and thematic art before gameplay begins. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.

The game flow connects title -> chapter select -> rooms -> chapter complete -> back to select without restarting the executable. All transitions are reachable through in-game UI. Score 0 if major transitions are missing or require relaunch.

During gameplay, dash charge state, death counter, and current room/chapter indicators are visible in a clear HUD that does not obstruct the play area. Score 0 if no HUD information is displayed during gameplay.

Readability at 1280x720 is strong: the player character, walls, hazards, and safe platforms are all clearly distinguishable. Hazard types are visually distinct from each other and from safe geometry. Score 0 if elements blend together or hazards are indistinguishable from platforms.

The art direction is coherent across title, rooms, hazards, character, and UI — a consistent crystalline-cavern or precision-platformer aesthetic with unified palette, typography, and visual hierarchy. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Room environments use real sprite or tile art for walls, platforms, backgrounds, and hazards — not plain ColorRect fills or default HTML 引擎 primitives. Different chapters have visually distinct themes. Score 0 if environments are uniform color fills or unstyled rectangles.

HUD and UI chrome: death counter, timer, chapter select, and results screens use styled themed widgets with custom panels, icon buttons, or themed StyleBox — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled default default widgets.

Animation and feedback: dash produces a trail or flash, death has a particle burst or screen shake, wall-cling shows sliding particles, and room transitions use motion rather than instant cuts. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
